note: Concrete CSS for rule actions. Direction of each effect comes from the evidence cited by the rules that use it. The MAGNITUDE (how much) is a design choice, kept deliberately modest, and must be tuned during the internal review (B11). Effects only use properties that cannot hide content, move elements or shrink targets (checked by tests). Saturation filters CAN lower text contrast (see contrastSimulation, a correction made in B8): every changed element is therefore checked at runtime by the accessibility guard, which undoes a rule that measurably worsens contrast, target size or horizontal scroll. Intensity (P3): each effect with a magnitude has three levels. `declarations` is Standard (the default, unchanged since B8); `levels.light` and `levels.strong` are weaker and stronger values chosen by the same design judgment: the direction always comes from the cited evidence, the size never does. Every level passes the same forbidden-property checks and the runtime accessibility guard.

effects.basis: Direction: Chinese homepages show higher visual density and more blocks (li2026); Chinese users prefer relatively high density (nng2016). Magnitude is a design choice.
constraints: Line height stays at or above 1.4 so text remains readable; no font-size change.
gap only affects flex/grid containers, so non-grid layouts are untouched.

effects.basis: Direction: Western homepages show lower visual density and fewer blocks (li2026); weak supporting evidence from nng2016 that foreign participants tolerated simple sites. Magnitude is a design choice.
constraints: No content is hidden; only spacing grows.

effects.basis: Direction: less white space on Chinese sites (li2022). Magnitude is a design choice.
constraints: Block padding only; interactive targets keep their own size.

effects.basis: Direction: more white space on Western sites (li2022). Magnitude is a design choice.
Direction: Chinese palettes are more saturated and brighter than Western ones (li2026). Magnitude is a design choice.
constraints: Hue is not changed (no red/gold stereotype).
Can lower text contrast on some colour pairs (see contrastSimulation): the runtime accessibility guard undoes the rule on any element where contrast measurably gets worse.

effects.basis: Direction: Chinese palettes are wider, more saturated, brighter (li2026), and use more red and blue (li2022). Magnitude is a design choice.
constraints: Can lower text contrast on some colour pairs (see contrastSimulation): the runtime accessibility guard undoes the rule on any element where contrast measurably gets worse.

effects.basis: Direction: higher image diversity and visual density on Chinese homepages (li2026). Card-level application is an extrapolation, so this effect is provisional. Magnitude is a design choice.
constraints: Images keep their alt text; no image is hidden or replaced.

effects.basis: Direction: more underlined links on Western sites (li2022). Underlining also keeps links identifiable without relying on colour (WCAG 1.4.1).
constraints: Applies to links inside the marked blocks only; buttons and navigation chrome are not blocks the rule targets.

effects.basis: Direction: promotions and carousels are more selective in Western designs (li2026 posters 66 vs 99, autoplay 39 vs 99). Weight is reduced through saturation, never opacity (opacity lowers contrast on every pair); saturation can still lower contrast on some pairs, so it is guarded at runtime. Magnitude is a design choice.
constraints: Content stays fully visible and readable; no opacity change.
Can lower text contrast on some colour pairs (see contrastSimulation): the runtime accessibility guard undoes the rule on any element where contrast measurably gets worse.

effects.basis: Direction: banners, carousels and recommendations carry more weight in Chinese designs (li2026, project synthesis). Magnitude is a design choice.
constraints: Can lower text contrast on some colour pairs (see contrastSimulation): the runtime accessibility guard undoes the rule on any element where contrast measurably gets worse.

effects.basis: Provisional: the rule using it (search first) is a hypothesis. An outline in the text colour marks the element without altering any colour or layout.
constraints: currentColor keeps contrast equal to the text; outline does not affect layout.

intentionallyEmpty.reason: Rule visual.western.strong-hierarchy is a hypothesis with no direct measurement of visual hierarchy. No effect is invented; it becomes active only when validated.
Rule visual.china.flat-hierarchy links block count to visual weight only by interpretation. No effect is invented until validated.

contrastSimulation.what: Share of text/background colour pairs that pass WCAG 4.5:1 and fall below it after the CSS saturate() filter.
contrastSimulation.method: All pairs of a 5x5x5 RGB grid (levels 0, 64, 128, 192, 255) with contrast >= 4.5 before; text and background both filtered (worst case: they belong to the same filtered element). Reproduced by tests/b8.test.ts.
contrastSimulation.correction: Until B7 this file claimed that saturation filters keep luminance and therefore do not lower contrast. That was wrong: the filter works on sRGB values, so relative luminance changes. The claim was removed and the runtime guard added.
contrastSimulation.caveat: Synthetic grid, not real pages; real sites use few distinct colours, so the real share is unknown until B11.
